chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the emancipation of the coerced, so he said: 'His emancipation is not (a valid) emancipation.'

key_terms.الْمُكْرَهِ: The coerced one (person forced against their will)
key_terms.عِتْق: Emancipation or manumission of a slave
key_terms.لَيْسَ عِتْقُهُ بِعِتْقٍ: His emancipation is not (considered) emancipation (i.e., invalid)

ai.seo_question: Is the self-emancipation of a coerced slave valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the manumission of a slave who is coerced (*mukrah*) is legally invalid, distinguishing it from voluntary emancipation. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that *ikrah* (coercion) negates the element of free will (*ikhtiyar*) required for valid legal acts (*fi'l*), ensuring that the slave's status remains unchanged until a genuine declaration of freedom is made.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about an emancipation of the coerced. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His emancipation is not with a (valid) emancipation’.
